html:
The Third Battle of Panipat was fought on 14 January 1761 between the army of the Maratha Confederacy and the Afghan king Ahmad Shah Durrani. It was one of the largest and bloodiest battles of the 18th century, and it ended the Maratha bid to rule all India.

By 1758 Maratha armies had reached Lahore and Attock. That brought them up against Ahmad Shah, who had invaded India four times already. He came again and was joined by the Afghan Rohillas and the nawab of Awadh. The Marathas had angered the Rajputs, Jats and Sikhs and found no allies.

A large Maratha army under Sadashivrao Bhau marched north with heavy guns and a crowd of pilgrims and families. In late 1760 the Afghans cut its supply road. For two months it starved in a fortified camp at Panipat.

On 14 January the Marathas attacked at dawn. Their guns and their trained infantry nearly broke the Afghan line. In the afternoon Ahmad Shah sent in his reserves and camel guns. The Peshwa's son was shot dead, Bhau rode into the fight and vanished, and the army collapsed. Tens of thousands died that day and thousands of prisoners were killed the next.

Ahmad Shah went home. The Marathas recovered within a decade, but the East India Company, which won at Buxar three years later, gained most.
